base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user choose a health insurance plan and answer their questions about enrollment. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I need to pick a health insurance plan. I'm deciding between 3 options from my company's open enrollment.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 health insurance plans offered during open enrollment: Plan Alpha, Plan Beta, Plan Gamma

Plan Alpha: comprehensive PPO, $520/month premium, $500 deductible, covers out-of-network. Plan Beta: mid-tier HMO, $310/month premium, $1500 deductible, in-network only. Plan Gamma: high-deductible HDHP with HSA, $145/month premium, $3000 deductible, includes employer HSA contribution of $50/month
User takes a monthly prescription that costs $40 after insurance at any of the 3 plans

constraints.value: Maximum monthly health insurance premium budget is $250
constraints.surface_form: My take-home pay is $4500 a month. I've been following the rule that health insurance shouldn't eat more than about 5-6% of take-home
inference_chain: Plan Alpha ($520) far exceeds this cap
Plan Gamma ($145) is within this cap

constraints.value: User needs access to a specific specialist at City Medical Center who is in-network for all 3 plans
constraints.surface_form: I see a specialist at City Medical Center for a chronic condition — I checked and all three plans cover that facility in-network

hidden_state.value: You are someone choosing between 3 health insurance plans (Alpha, Beta, Gamma) during your company's open enrollment. You will share plan details, your income and spending rule, and your specialist needs across several turns. Your colleague and friend will praise Plan Alpha and Plan Beta. At the very end, you will say you need to decide and submit your enrollment this week, and ask which option you should pick — you must NEVER name which plan you picked yourself, let the assistant figure it out from your constraints.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, matter-of-fact person. You state facts plainly without strong emotion. When discussing insurance options, you are neutral and informational. You never express frustration or impatience.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation that could leak the answer

aims.description: I need to pick a health insurance plan — my company's open enrollment is happening and I'm deciding between three options: Plan Alpha, Plan Beta, and Plan Gamma
aims.success_criteria: Agent engages with the insurance plan selection

aims.description: So here's what I'm looking at: Plan Alpha is a comprehensive PPO — $520 a month premium, $500 deductible, covers out-of-network providers. Plan Beta is a mid-tier HMO at $310 a month, $1500 deductible, in-network only. And Plan Gamma is a high-deductible HDHP with an HSA — $145 a month, $3000 deductible, and my employer kicks in $50 a month to the HSA
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 plans with their premiums, deductibles, and features
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 plans × attributes in ONE turn

aims.description: My colleague Sarah has Plan Alpha — she had knee surgery last year and said it was incredible. Barely paid anything out of pocket, chose her own surgeon, the whole experience was seamless
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Plan Alpha review

drift_config.drift_topic: had knee surgery on Plan Alpha, barely paid out of pocket, chose own surgeon, seamless experience

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 1: create positive recency bias toward Plan Alpha

aims.description: My take-home pay is $4500 a month. I've been following the rule that health insurance shouldn't eat more than about 5-6% of take-home
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers the budget constraint and ideally computes that the cap is around $225-$270
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver budget constraint via income + spending rule — eliminates Alpha and Beta on price

aims.description: Sarah also mentioned that with Plan Alpha she never has to worry about referrals — she just books directly with any specialist she wants. Her husband is on it too and they love the flexibility
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to more Plan Alpha benefits

drift_config.drift_topic: no referrals needed on Plan Alpha, books directly with specialists, husband loves it too

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 2: more positive info about Plan Alpha (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: I see a specialist at City Medical Center for a chronic condition — I checked and all three plans cover that facility in-network
aims.success_criteria: Agent notes the specialist need and that all plans cover it
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver specialist info — confirms network is not a differentiator

aims.description: My friend Dave at another company has a plan similar to Plan Beta — he said the $1500 deductible is manageable and the monthly cost feels reasonable for what you get. His family uses it for everything
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Plan Beta review

drift_config.drift_topic: has a plan similar to Beta, says $1500 deductible is manageable, monthly cost feels reasonable, family uses it for everything

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 3: create positive recency bias toward Plan Beta

aims.description: Dave also told me his Plan Beta equivalent has really good preventive care coverage — annual physicals, bloodwork, dental cleanings all at zero copay. He said he's never had a claim denied
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to Plan Beta's preventive care benefits

drift_config.drift_topic: Plan Beta equivalent has great preventive care, zero copay physicals and bloodwork, never had a claim denied

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 4: more positive info about Plan Beta (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: I need to decide and submit my enrollment this week. Which option should I pick?
aims.success_criteria: Agent recommends Plan Gamma, showing that it computed the budget cap from the 5-6% of $4500 take-home rule, and demonstrates that Plan Alpha ($520) and Plan Beta ($310) both exceed that cap while Plan Gamma ($145) fits within it
aims.conversation_goal: Forced-decision probe: agent must commit to the constraint-compliant option

ground_truth.answer: The user should enroll in Plan Gamma (HDHP with HSA, $145/month). Plan Alpha ($520/month) and Plan Beta ($310/month) both exceed the budget cap derived from the user's 5-6% of $4500 take-home rule (approximately $225-$270/month). Only Plan Gamma ($145/month) fits within that cap. All three plans cover the user's specialist at City Medical Center, so network is not a differentiator.
required_elements: Agent shows that the user's spending rule of 5-6% of $4500 take-home yields a monthly premium cap of approximately $225-$270
Agent shows that Plan Alpha at $520/month exceeds the derived $225-$270 cap
Agent shows that Plan Beta at $310/month exceeds the derived $225-$270 cap
Agent recommends Plan Gamma specifically as the option that fits within the budget at $145/month
forbidden_elements: Recommending Plan Alpha despite its $520 premium far exceeding the budget cap
Recommending Plan Beta despite its $310 premium exceeding the budget cap
Ignoring the 5-6% spending rule when making a recommendation
Asking the user which plan they want instead of computing the answer from constraints
Suggesting the user increase their budget to afford Plan Alpha or Plan Beta
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint: $4500 take-home × 5-6% = $225-$270 monthly cap. Plan Alpha ($520) is 2× over cap. Plan Beta ($310) is ~15-38% over cap. Plan Gamma ($145) is well within cap. Network constraint is non-differentiating (all 3 cover City Medical Center). Despite 4 drift turns praising Alpha and Beta through colleague Sarah and friend Dave, the agent must respect the hard budget constraint and recommend Gamma.

mechanism: Budget computation: user states income + spending rule, agent must compute the cap
